speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better understand your condition, how old are you and do you have any history of gout, psoriasis, or kidney disease? Additionally, has the right knee pain been constant or does it come in episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Uric_Acid_Level. Given your age, sexual history, and symptoms of knee swelling with urinary pain, we need to rule out a reactive arthritis or gonococcal infection. Have you noticed any eye redness or discharge recently?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein: Negative, Blood: Negative, WBC: 12–16/hpf, RBC: 1–2/hpf; Uric_Acid_Level: Not recorded in provided data.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis. The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), urethritis (pain with urination), and your sexual history is classic for Reactive Arthritis, often triggered by an asymptomatic STI. Multiple sclerosis does not present with acute monoarticular joint swelling and urinary pain in this manner. Please confirm if you have any history of eye redness or pain, and request an urgent Urinalysis and Uric_Acid_Level to confirm inflammation and rule out gout.
